chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from his father Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Naṣīb (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) when he leads us in prayer: 'What do you say about the prayer with him?' He said, 'As for if he recites aloud, then be silent to the Quran and listen, then bow and prostrate; you are praying for yourself.'

Thus it does not contradict the first report, because in the report there is no command to be silent nor a prohibition against recitation, and it is not impossible that it is obligatory upon him to be silent to the recitation, and with this, recitation is incumbent upon him for himself. And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَنْتَ لِنَفْسِكَ: You are for yourself (your prayer is valid independently).
key_terms.اَلنَّاصِبِ: Naṣīb: One who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, often used to describe the Umayyads or their followers in Shia theology.
key_terms.فَأَنْصِتْ لِلْقُرْآنِ: Then be silent to the Quran (do not recite while he recites aloud).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind a Naṣīb when he recites the Quran aloud?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the validity of congregational prayer behind a *Naṣīb* (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) by clarifying that the follower's silence during the Imam's loud recitation does not invalidate their own prayer. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the obligation to listen (*inṣāt*) and the act of recitation, allowing the follower to recite silently for themselves while remaining attentive to the Imam, thereby resolving apparent contradictions with other reports. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the spiritual status of the Imam is not a strict condition for the validity of the prayer behind him, provided the essential pillars are fulfilled.
